newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt rises, led by high-yielding countries.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt rises, led by high-yielding countries.

text.p: Most emerging market debt prices climbed on Tuesday in moderate trading dominated by dealer activity, market experts said.

"It was mainly a trader's market," a head Brady bond trader said. "It's probably a combination of the fact that there were shorts out, as well as people trying to call the low on the (U.S.) Treasury market."
The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield has held near 6.50 percent so far this week after prices slid sharply Friday, prompting some investors to bet on a rebound.
Tuesday's emerging market debt gains centered largely in such high-yielders as Peru, Ecuador and Russia.
Peru PDIs rose 7/8 to 65-1/2, their spreads tightening about 22 basis points to comparable Treasuries.

Traders attributed the gains to stronger-than-expected gross domestic product figures released Tuesday. Peru's GDP grew 8.2 percent year-on-year in June, compared with 5.1 percent year-on-year growth in the same month last year. Analysts had forecast a figure closer to 7.0 percent.
Ecuador Discounts rose 1/2 to 78-1/2 as retail clients stepped into the credit, traders said.
"Ecuador started to see a little more retail buying, Peru is more the Street," one trader said.
Russian Vnesh loans continued to benefit from anticipation of the country's debt restructuring, expected to close in October or November, dealers said.
Brady debt from other, more-mainstream issuers rose less markedly. Argentina Pars rose 1/8 to 74-5/8, Brazil "C" bonds climbed 1/4 to 83-1/4 bid and Mexico pars were up 3/8 at 81-1/2.
Because U.S. Treasuries prices turned modestly lower, yields spreads tightened for nearly all emerging market issues. Ecuador, Bulgaria and Peru narrowed most significantly.
